messages:
maya: fyi customer BrightEdge on eu-west-2 dedicated pool reports sudden 429 bursts + auth errors during heavy traffic window (13:24Z). They think it's tied to another tenant on same host. attaching initial traces below.

sam: thanks — can you paste a few request_ids and the pool/node id?

maya: request_ids: req_8f3e2, req_8f3e9, req_8f402. node: eu2-ded-3f. logs: ```2026-03-15T13:24:02Z req_8f3e2 429 throttler queued_latency_ms=3200 route=/v1/generate tenant=brightedge
2026-03-15T13:24:03Z req_8f3e2 auth=ERR signature_missing
2026-03-15T13:24:04Z req_8f3e9 200 model=gpt-j-6b token_cost=123
2026-03-15T13:24:05Z req_8f402 429 throttler queued_latency_ms=4100```.

ivan: queued_latency_ms > 3000 is our throttler cutoff for the pool. But the auth error is odd — maybe a downstream timeout caused the SDK to retry with bad header?

zara: i pulled node metrics around that time — see snippet: ```gpu0_sm: 95% gpu1_sm: 12% slice3_sm: 98% slice1_sm: 20% memory_util: 83%``` looks like one MIG slice saturated while others idle.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled up +2 gpus (eu2-ded-3f) at 2026-03-15T13:24:10Z due to p95_latency breach.

oncall-ml: observed bursty SM saturation on slice 3 for ~90s. NV link traffic also spiked. This matches noisy-neighbor contention rather than systemic auth.

maya: customer also reported a billing delta — cost spike for the same minute. could be retries.

sam: action plan: 1) repro on eu2-ded-3f with synthetic harness; 2) collect nvidia-smi dmon / perf counters; 3) check MIG partition mapping and fractional packing policy for that node; 4) consider live-migrate tenant if repro confirms.

ivan: repro command I used: ```ab-test --concurrency 24 --seq-len 512 --model gpt-j-6b --duration 120 --target-node eu2-ded-3f``` running now, will post perf counters.

zara: quick check: kube scheduling shows fractional_packing=true and max_slices_per_gpu=4 on that node. Tenant BrightEdge was on slice 3 with another large tenant on slice 3 too (overscheduled).

oncall-ml: tentative hypothesis: fractional packing + aggressive autoscale caused two large jobs to land on same physical GPU slices (MIG slice overlap), producing SM-level contention spikes that pushed queued latency > throttler threshold and triggered retries. Auth error likely a side-effect of timeout/retry path.

sam: mitigation for now: set pool policy to strict_isolation for BrightEdge, set max_burst to 1, and schedule a one-off move to an empty node. Can infra do immediate migration?

infra-bot: migration job queued: migrate tenant BrightEdge -> eu2-ded-4a, expected finish 2026-03-15T13:27:45Z.

maya: i've told customer we'll move them and follow up with root-cause. leaving repro harness running to capture counters.

oncall-ml: attaching quick perf snapshot from repro: ```SM_util_slice3: 99% cycles, warp_stalls_mem: high, l2_hit_rate: 65%, nvlink_tx: 1.2GB/s```.

ivan: recommendation: add an admission check to avoid co-locating >1 large-slice tenant per physical GPU for fractional_packing pools. Also log an event when throttler trips so we can trace to co-residency.

zara: opened infra ticket INF-2026-291 to change packing policy defaults and add throttler->cohost tagging.

sam: thanks team. i'll draft a short incident note for the customer explaining noisy neighbor interactions, the migration, and the follow-up infra work. maya pls confirm once migration completes. :thumbsup:

maya: migration finished at 2026-03-15T13:27:43Z, BrightEdge reports error rate down to normal. keeping thread open for post-mortem notes.
